chapter_title: Concerning the Fifty Lord's Days; to what Mysteries do they correspond? Or the Second (Fifty); to whose Sign (are they)?
chapter_note: The chapter opens with a late Q&A frame about catechumen/elect fasting. The oldest layer appears in the central computation-mapping: five garments × five powers → twenty-five limbs/sons, tied to the hypostases Summons/Answer/Obedience and the ascent mechanism. The second half shows strong editorial fatigue: institutional categories (catechumens/elect/church) and then explicit NT-derived narrative justifications (Christ’s desert fasting, Simon the leper, tomb), which are overlay/pastoral rather than substrate.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic Q&A container (“Once again… disciple… I beseech you, my master… proclaim… persuade us”) plus institutional fasting categories (catechumens/elect). This functions as editorial apparatus rather than cosmological exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: Happen you know that [in eac]h one of these five garments that the [First] Man summoned there are five powers. They shall be counted to the [ ... each] other, these five, and five times [ ... ] their number. However, at the time [ ... ] the Summons went down. The Answer wished to ascend with it. And the Summons with the Obedience [constitute] twenty-five characteristics in their twenty-five limbs, [which] are the sons of the Man. The Summons and [the Obed]ience were raised to the heights through them.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the dialogue attribution/frame clause: “Then [he] says to his questioner and they with him:” (Layer-2 Q&A framing).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core teaching marked by systematic numeric correspondences (five garments × five powers = twenty-five), and by intra-cosmic hypostases acting as agents (Summons/Answer/Obedience) with ascent mechanics; only the initial speaking formula is later frame.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.263⟩ Just as their fa[ther] the living Man raised himself up through them, by these these other ones have set up all things a[bov]e and below. Indeed, these are what are called pentecost, the fifty great days that are the [archetypes of the] holy [d]ays. They fasted from their [foo]d, [w]hich is their own.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological causality and archetype language: ascent of the Living Man through the limbs/sons, and ‘fifty’ treated as a structural/archetypal measure within the system (not yet tied to church practice or NT narrative).

paragraphs.core_text: So, from that time until [the time] of [the adv]ent of Jesus the Splendour, the glorious one who came [ ... / ... t]heir food which is the [ ... ] of sou[l], which is the Summons and the Obedience [ ... ] that spiritual food. They rele[ased ... ] all these fifty days, which [ ... ] this living food suffices for all of them. It filled them all with power and richness and life. Light [ ... ] this living food that [ ... ] became rich.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same intra-cosmic mechanism: ‘food of soul’ identified with hypostases (Summons/Obedience) and described as living/spiritual nourishment. “Jesus the Splendour” functions as a cosmological figure, not as a Gospel citation.

Institutionalization of the scheme: ‘catechumens’ and ‘elect’ fasting practice, counting of “holy days,” and liturgical scheduling. This applies the earlier cosmological arithmetic to church groups—cosmos → institution.

Explicitly anchors the practice in ecclesial revelation and polemic against ‘sects,’ then grounds it in apostolic precedent (“apostles themselves fasted…”). This is Christian-historical legitimization language entering via the NT/Christian milieu rather than the old cosmological substrate.
Direct NT narrative material (temptation scene, Simon the leper, time in the tomb). This entered via Gospel tradition, regardless of any numerological/correspondential use.

First-person bestowal onto ‘the entire church’ with catechumen/elect differentiation—an editorial application of the mysteries to institutional practice (cosmos → church). The paragraph’s function is ecclesial assignment rather than cosmological exposition.
